_note: One capture, several regions. The capture is the whole swapchain after the
UI pass, which is what makes it evidence for the paint layer and also what
makes whole-image comparison worthless: it contains a ReSTIR-lit viewport
that is stochastic by construction, an fps counter that changes every
frame, and whatever toast happened to be up. Every region below is chrome
Thresholds are tight but not exact. Byte-identity is the right bar for a
draw list (GHOSTFENCE row 1 asserts that separately, on instance counts);
it is the wrong bar for a rasterised image, where a driver update can move
a subpixel without anything being wrong.

images.name: menu-bar
why: The logo, the wordmark and six menu labels. Pure text and one SDF icon,
on a flat fill — which makes it the most sensitive region in the shell
to a change in glyph rasterisation, and therefore the region that
decides the MORROWIND-G shaper A/B (plan Appendix A.5, item 2).
Deliberately stops at x=430, well left of the command palette, because
the palette carries a focus ring whose state is not load-deterministic.

images.name: sculpt-panel
why: Six tool rows: an SDF icon, a label, a row background and the selected
row's wash. This is the Phase 27 paint contract's rounded / washed /
lifted primitives in one place, at the size they actually ship at.
Stops at h=200 rather than running to the bottom of the panel because
the lower rows sit against the content drawer's top edge, which moves

images.name: toolbar
why: Save / Select / Landscape / Foliage and the four play-control glyphs.
Icon-and-label pairs at toolbar size, where a half-pixel of icon
drift is visible and a half-pixel of text drift is not — the two
failure modes the block-origin snapping rule trades between.
